title: Hot Chocolate Oatmeal

items: 35 grams oats, I use rolled oats
120 ml milk , any works here - almond, lactose free, oat or regular
1/2 - 1 tbsp cocoa powder, use a good quality one
1 tsp jaggery or your prefered sweetener of choice ( monkfruit, maple syrup, regular sugar )
optional: 1 square dark chocolate if you want it to be extract chocolatelyyy <3

method: In a pot, add in the oats, milk and water
Cook for 10 minutes then add in the cocoa powder and jaggery ( optional )
Cook till you get the desired consistency
Top with fruit of choice, some dark chocolate and a small teaspoon of peanut butter
This oatmeal recipe yields a single serving, but it’s easily scalable for larger quantities, perfect for meal prepping or serving the whole family. Just adjust the ingredient amounts accordingly.
Opt for a high-quality dark chocolate or baking bar when incorporating dark chocolate into the recipe. Avoid using chocolate chips as they don’t melt as smoothly or yield the same consistency.

Hot Chocolate Oatmeal

Nutrition: 
C: 61 | F: 18 | P: 14
Calories: 442 per serve 
Makes 1 serving

Ingredients
35 grams oats, I use rolled oats
120 ml milk , any works here - almond, lactose free, oat or regular 
120 ml water
1/2 - 1 tbsp cocoa powder, use a good quality one 
pinch of salt
1 tsp jaggery or your prefered sweetener of choice ( monkfruit, maple syrup, regular sugar )
drop of vanilla extract 
optional: 1 square dark chocolate if you want it to be extract chocolatelyyy <3 

toppings
strawberries
70% dark chocolate cube 
1 tsp peanut butter
crunchy granola, optional, for crunch 

Method
in a pot, add in the oats, milk and water
cook for 10 minutes then add in the cocoa powder and jaggery ( optional ) 
cook till you get the desired consistency
top with fruit of choice, some dark chocolate and a small teaspoon of peanut butter

recipe notes
this oatmeal recipe yields a single serving, but it’s easily scalable for larger quantities, perfect for meal prepping or serving the whole family. Just adjust the ingredient amounts accordingly.
opt for a high-quality dark chocolate or baking bar when incorporating dark chocolate into the recipe. Avoid using chocolate chips as they don’t melt as smoothly or yield the same consistency.
